response: {"headline": "PROVE IT-TIMI 22 met its primary endpoint with a 21% relative risk reduction (p=0.005) but the benefit was narrower than a robust success due to low statistical power and a liver safety signal with high-dose atorvastatin.", "summary": "The trial randomized 4,162 ACS patients to atorvastatin 80 mg or pravastatin 40 mg for a median of 2 years. The primary composite endpoint (death, MI, unstable angina, late revascularization, stroke) occurred in 22.4% vs 26.3% (HR ~0.85, p=0.005). The calculator predicted HR 0.864 using a within-arm LDL-C reduction of 46.2% from a phase 2 study, which closely matches the observed effect. However, the trial had only 64% power (MDE HR 0.839 vs expected 0.864), meaning the upper confidence bound likely approaches 1.0 and does not meet the \"robust\" threshold. A safety signal showed more liver-related adverse events with high-dose atorvastatin (3.3% vs 1.1%). At the 2004 cut-off, HMGCR genetic evidence was not yet published (score 0.695 but zero pre-cutoff studies), leaving target genetics formally uncertain. The result is a narrow success: the effect is real and mechanism-consistent but statistically fragile and accompanied by a dose-related safety signal.", "key_evidence": ["Primary endpoint met: p=0.005, event rates 22.4% vs 26.3% (21% RRR) — New Study Demonstrates The Benefits Of Intensive Statin Therapy In Patients Hospitalized With Acute Coronary Syndrome", "Trial size and follow-up: 4,162 randomized, 2-year median follow-up — New Study Demonstrates The Benefits Of Intensive Statin Therapy In Patients Hospitalized With Acute Coronary Syndrome", "Calculator prediction: expected HR 0.864 (LDL-C equivalent 0.924 mmol/L, within-arm -46.2% from phase 2) — calculator output", "Liver safety signal: 3.3% vs 1.1% liver-related side effects — New Study Demonstrates The Benefits Of Intensive Statin Therapy In Patients Hospitalized With Acute Coronary Syndrome", "Target genetics uncertain: HMGCR score 0.695 but evidence_before_cutoff=0 — opentargets:HMGCR", "Benefit across LDL subgroups: ≥125 mg/dL 28.2% vs 20.1%; <125 mg/dL 25.6% vs 23.5% — New Study Demonstrates The Benefits Of Intensive Statin Therapy In Patients Hospitalized With Acute Coronary Syndrome"], "what_would_change_this": "Full publication confidence interval confirming upper bound well below 0.90 would upgrade to robust_success; long-term safety data showing the liver signal does not offset net benefit would resolve the caveat.", "readthrough_note": "The result supports intensive statin therapy in ACS; read-through to other high-dose statin programmes (e.g., SPARCL in stroke) is positive but each population needs its own safety assessment."}
